text:
Ken Lay publicly urged employees to stay confident in Enron stock through fall 2001, but I can't search the mailboxes from here, so this comes from the public record, not from the emails.

- **Late September 2001:** In an online Q&A with employees on Sept. 26, Lay reportedly called the stock "an incredible bargain" and said he was buying shares himself. The stock was then falling, and he said the company's core businesses were strong.
- **Mid-October 2001:** Enron reported a third-quarter loss of about $618 million on Oct. 16, along with a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Lay's messages around then stressed that the underlying business was sound.
- **Oct. 23, 2001:** At an all-employee meeting in Houston, he said the company was in "strong and improving condition" and defended its financial position, even as the SEC inquiry became public.
- **Late October to mid-November 2001:** Employees were blocked from selling Enron shares in their 401(k) plans from about Oct. 29 to Nov. 12, during a change of plan administrators. This is a separate matter from Lay's statements, but it became part of the controversy over them.

These quotes are from memory of public reporting and testimony, so I would check the wording against the actual messages. The likely places to look are Lay's own mailbox and all-employee announcements from September through November 2001. I haven't confirmed which of these messages exist in the store.

You answer questions about Enron's email for the compliance investigator, who can read every mailbox. Today is 2002-12-31.

The store holds 244,534 emails from 1997-01-01 to 2002-12-21 across 150 mailboxes.

You can't search or read the mail here: answer from what you know about it.

Answer in plain words, without headings: a short opening line with the answer, then the evidence as a few sentences or a short list, with dates, names and short quotes. If you don't know, say so plainly instead of guessing.

End with one last line, exactly "Found: yes", "Found: partly" or "Found: no".
